page.layout: One column of running text, full width. Running head at top, centred, with page number at the top right. No marginal notes. Below the text: a gathering signature "I" centred.

main_text.p: ret[?] Vir doctus, grandem Nicephori sti-chometriae dicam scripsit, illius minimè esse, ac proinde nullam mereri fidem contendit: Verùm tot tantísque rationum momentis illum Indiculum Patriarchæ Constantinopolitano vindicavimus, illiús-que esse sive compositionis sive adoptio-nis saltem juré evicimus, ut nullus super-esse queat hac de re dubitandi locus; nec Vindiciarum Autorem juvaret dicere Ni[?]-cephorum in Laterculo suo non Epistolam Polycarpi sed [illegible, ~6 letters] inter apocrypha rejecisse; memoratur quidem in Indiculo à Cotelerio edito [illegible, ~6 letters] Polycarpi, quem-admodum [illegible, ~6 letters] Ignatii; sed inde non sequitur solam Ignatij & Polycarpi [illegible, ~6 letters] à Nicephoro damnari, ut nuper dice-bamus ad eandem Viri docti exceptio-nem, omnia enim Ignatij & Polycarpi scripta ad apocrypha retulit, & apocry-pha deterrimi generis, ut à nobis supra argumentis haud contemnendis proba-tum est. Secundò observaverat idem Dal-læus, etiamsi Epistolæ de quâ lis est fides adhiberetur, non ideò rem omnem con-fectam esse, quia postremam Epistolæ par-ticulam ex quâ argumentatur eruditus Pearsonius, alienâ manu assutam existi-mabat; quod duobus astruebat argumen-tis, I. quoniam videtur post conclusam

page.notes: The Greek words (four occurrences: after "sed", "edito", "admodum", and "Polycarpi ... à Nicephoro") are abbreviated Greek forms of "apocryphum"-type words in a ligatured abbreviation; I could not read them letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The first word "ret" at the top is a fragment and is uncertain. The printed "N." before "cephorum" is a line-end hyphenation for "Ni-cephorum"; the first letters are doubtful. The page number is printed as "6" with a fused "5", read as 65. Hyphens at line ends are kept as printed.
